newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea prices rise on growing demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea prices rise on growing demand.

text.p: Prices rose at the Colombo auction on Wednesday, fuelled by the early stages of winter buying, brokers said.
"There was good demand. And we expect demand to grow further in the coming weeks when people start buying quantities for winter," said Rohan Iddawela of brokers Forbes and Walker.
Anticipated gross auction average for the 5.9 million kg on offer was 118 rupees per kg, up from the previous week's 116.33, Forbes said.
Quantities offered had been high over the past few weeks, boosted by fair weather in the growing areas.
"We expect the increased quantities to be absorbed at fairly satisfactory prices," Iddawela said.
The island's distinct low-grown teas, popular with Russian and Middle East buyers, met good demand with most varieties gaining two to four rupees, brokers said.
Most varieties of the more expensive high growns also gained while most western BOP fannings lost three to five rupees.
The next auction is on June 10-11, when 5.6 million kg will be on offer. (1$= 58.64) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
